source_refs.note: Exercise 1.2, Question 3 (book p. 14): pick the fundamental transcendental functions; answer key p. 297

blocks.prompt: 3. Which of the following functions are fundamental transcendental functions? \(f(x) = e^{x} + \cos x\), \(g(x) = \sin x\), \(h(x) = e^{2x}\), \(k(x) = \frac{e^{x}-e^{-x}}{2}\), \(r(x) = 15^{x}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan paanchon functions transcendental hain; humein in mein se fundamental (bunyadi) wale chunne hain.
Diya kya hai? Paanch transcendental functions.
Find kya karna hai? Kaun se fundamental transcendental hain.
Kaunsa rule? 1.3.1 aur 1.3.2: fundamental woh hain jo khud ek standard function hon, jaise \(a^{x}\) (\(a > 0, a \ne 1\)), \(\ln x\), \(\sin x\), \(\sin^{-1} x\). Jama, zarb, algebraic functions ke saath mel, ya composition (ek function ke andar doosra) se bane hue non-fundamental hain. Kitab ka apna test: \(10^{2x}\) fundamental hai kyun ke yeh \(100^{x}\) hai.
Plan: har function ko ek hi standard function ki shakal mein likhne ki koshish karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = e^{x} + \cos x\), \(g(x) = \sin x\), \(h(x) = e^{2x}\), \(k(x) = \frac{e^{x}-e^{-x}}{2}\), \(r(x) = 15^{x}\).
Maloom karna: fundamental transcendental functions kaun se hain.
Tareeqa: har function ko ek akele standard function ki shakal mein likhne ki koshish karenge. Agar ho jaye to fundamental; agar sirf kai functions ke mel ki shakal mein hi likha ja sake to non-fundamental.

\(f(x) = e^{x} + \cos x\)
Non-fundamental.
Kyun: yeh do alag transcendental functions (\(e^{x}\) aur \(\cos x\)) ka jama hai. Koi ek standard function iske barabar nahin, is liye yeh "bana hua" (combined) function hai.

\(g(x) = \sin x\)
Fundamental.
Kyun: \(\sin x\) un standard functions mein se hai jin ka naam 1.3.1 mein khud liya gaya hai. Is mein na koi jama hai, na zarb, na kisi function ke andar doosra function; yeh khud ek bunyadi eent (building block) hai jis se baqi functions bante hain.

\(h(x) = e^{2x}\)
\[e^{2x} = \left(e^{2}\right)^{x} = a^{x}\]
\[a = e^{2} \approx 7.389\]
Fundamental.
Kyun: exponents ke qaide \(a^{mn} = (a^{m})^{n}\) se \(e^{2x}\) ek akela exponential \(a^{x}\) ban gaya, jahan \(a = e^{2} > 0\) aur \(a \ne 1\). Bilkul kitab ki misaal \(10^{2x} = 100^{x}\) ki tarah.
Dhyan dein: "2x" dekh kar ise composition samajhna aam ghalti hai; kitab ka rule ise fundamental maanta hai.

\(k(x) = \frac{e^{x}-e^{-x}}{2}\)
Non-fundamental.
Kyun: yeh do exponentials \(e^{x}\) aur \(e^{-x}\) ka mel hai (pehle farq, phir aadha). Ise ek akeli power \(a^{x}\) ki shakal mein nahin likha ja sakta.

\(r(x) = 15^{x}\)
Fundamental.
Kyun: yeh seedha \(a^{x}\) hai, jahan \(a = 15 > 0\) aur \(a \ne 1\). Base kitna bhi bara ho, jab tak woh positive aur 1 ke ilawa hai, \(a^{x}\) fundamental exponential function hi rehta hai.

Tasdeeq: answer key bhi \(g\), \(h\) aur \(r\) batati hai. Jawab mil gaya. Yaad rakhne ka fori test: function ko ek akeli power \(a^{x}\) (ya ek akela standard function) bana sako to fundamental, warna non-fundamental.
blocks.final_answer: Fundamental transcendental functions \(g(x) = \sin x\), \(h(x) = e^{2x}\) aur \(r(x) = 15^{x}\) hain. (\(f\) aur \(k\) non-fundamental hain.)
